title: Retrospective Evaluation of clinicopathologic correlations and genetic analysis in patients with Tumor Induced Osteomalacia (TIO)
summary:
Tumor-induced osteomalacia (TIO) is a very rare disease in which a usually benign tumor disrupts the body's phosphate balance. This can lead to bone pain, muscle weakness, fatigue, and fractures. The aim of this study is to improve our understanding of this rare condition.

The study will analyze existing medical records, tissue samples, laboratory results, imaging studies, and surgical findings from patients with TIO. No additional examinations, blood samples, or study visits are required. The results may help improve the diagnosis of this rare disease and support earlier and more effective treatment for future patients.

interventions.name: Retrospective cohort of patients with histologically confirmed phosphaturic mesenchymal tumors (PMTs) and clinically documented tumor-induced osteomalacia (TIO). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor (PMT).
Clinically and biochemically confirmed tumor-induced osteomalacia (TIO).
Availability of complete histopathological and clinical routine data, including imaging and surgical documentation.
Exclusion criteria:
Missing or insufficient histopathological or clinical records preventing assessment of the primary study endpoints.
Tumors without evidence of tumor-induced osteomalacia or without histological confirmation of a phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor.
